title: Lattice component manifest
description: Spec + prose source-of-truth for a Lattice layout. The engine reads name/function/form/substance/skeleton/slots/variants. The build-component-docs.js generator reads the prose fields (description, purpose, whenToUse, antiPatterns, related, variantDocs) to emit <name>.docs.md and <name>.gallery.md. See design/design-system.md.

function.description: Audience-function family the component belongs to (what the viewer leaves knowing). One of the seven taxonomies in design/design-system.md §3.

bucket.description: Disk-layout bucket the component lives in under lib/components/<bucket>/<name>/. Defaults to the value of `function` when absent. Four substance-defined buckets (`chart` for data visualizations, `diagram` for topological visuals, `math` for typeset equations, `code` for syntax-highlighted source) and one domain-defined bucket (`legal` for legal-family components) override the function value when colocation aids maintenance — each substance bucket describes a category of rendered content, not the library that happens to render it today. See design/design-system.md §9.

galleryAuthored.description: When true, the build-component-docs.js generator skips writing <name>.gallery.md (the file is hand-authored). Use this for components where variation lives in slide CONTENT, not in modifier classes — e.g. `diagram` (every Mermaid diagram type is the same _class) or future `code`/`math` if their galleries need a richer showcase than the manifest's variantDocs can express. <name>.docs.md is still generated from the manifest. The integration test continues to assert light/dark page-count parity for the PDFs but no longer derives the expected count from the manifest formula.

stage.description: How this component's stage Cell is sized under the Form default (design/forms.md; engineering/decisions/2026-07-14-one-frame-model.md). `flow` = a flowing prose/structure body that the masthead kernel wraps in a bounded `.cell-stage` clip cell (the overflow probe walls it). `canvas` = a self-sizing body (a chart's `.chart-body`, a Mermaid SVG, a QR/poster card) that measures against its own box and keeps a direct-child body — the stage Cell is that box, not a generic wrapper. OMITTED for sovereign frames (title/divider/closing/image/split-panel/split-compare/math/compare-code), whose stage is their own grid and which are chrome-exempt (frame.kind:sovereign, derived from lib/forms/frame/*). The three-way {flow, canvas, sovereign} classification is the single source the stage-catalog generator composes; masthead.transform.js derives its wrap decision from it.

conformance.description: OPT-IN to the frame-conformance gate (engineering/decisions/2026-07-15-model-driven-frame-render.md §2). When set to `strict`, the conformance test renders this component under the Form default and asserts its rendered cell tree equals its declared model — every declared frame Cell materialized, every present slot hoisted into its Cell, nothing loose, no dead `> .cell-stage` selector. OMIT to stay on the fail-safe default path (today's `wrapsStageBody` behavior) until the component is migrated. Per-component opt-in is deliberate: the gate can only go green one conforming component at a time (a global flip would be red until all 56 conform — a monster branch, HARD RULE #17/#18). The migration flips this flag as its last step, once the render is proven byte-identical AND the overflow-probe verdict + autosplit decisions are proven unchanged (§5, the PROTECTED measuring machinery).

orientation.description: The canvas orientations this component is DESIGNED for — a bidirectional support contract. `["landscape","portrait"]` = both (most layouts: native scaling or explicit reflow); `["landscape"]` = landscape-only (e.g. redline's side-by-side diff); `["portrait"]` = portrait/social-only (built for the vertical feed). lint:deck warns when a deck's @size orientation is NOT in this list — in either direction. Default (omitted) = both. How a 'both' layout adapts to portrait (native vs reflow) is recorded in the audit notes, not here. See engineering/decisions/2026-06-16-orientation-in-the-form-model.md.

adapt.description: Adaptivity declaration (engineering/decisions/2026-06-20-adaptive-manifest-contract.md). `mode` is the REQUIRED, deterministic statement of how the layout handles non-landscape boxes; every component declares one. `families` and the rest are the box-local reflow CONTRACT — the honest support list + declared layout INTENT the authored per-family CSS honors (the data a future resolver would consume without re-authoring). The CSS is hand-written (#2 'authored per family'); this block does NOT generate layout. NOTE: distinct from the top-level `families` field, which names opt-in modifier groups (e.g. state-markers).

mode.description: How the component adapts to the box/orientation it occupies. `reflow` = ships DISTINCT per-family structural layouts (via `@container lattice (aspect-ratio …)` CSS, a `*.transform.js` that branches geometry on orientation, or the mermaid reorient) — the box is restructured, not just scaled. `native` = adapts by the universal cqi scaling + orientation-aware type alone, no structural change needed (most prose/figure layouts). `single-orientation` = deliberately ONE orientation (its `orientation` field has one entry), e.g. redline's side-by-side diff. A CI gate (tools/check-ownership.js checkAdaptDeclarations) cross-checks the declaration against reality: any component whose CSS carries `@container … aspect-ratio` MUST be `reflow`, so the declaration can never silently drift from the code.

families.description: The box-FAMILIES this component ships authored layouts for — the finer, box-local successor to `orientation`. A component reflows box-locally via `@container lattice (aspect-ratio …)`, so it adapts to the box it OCCUPIES (a portrait deck, OR a narrow nested cell), not just the deck. Four families by container aspect: `wide` (>1.05) · `square` (0.9–1.05) · `tall` (0.5–0.9) · `strip` (<0.5). Omitted = derived from `orientation` (landscape→[wide,square], portrait→[tall,strip]) so unmigrated components stay honest. Render-backed: set it only once the authored layouts are verified.

priority.description: Slots / content roles in importance order, highest first — what leads and what sheds first when the box can't hold everything. Slot names SHOULD be keys of `slots`; sub-part role names are free-form (documented in the component's docs).

droppable.description: Sub-parts the layout may SHED in the narrowest (strip) family — tightest last. Each is a role the authored strip CSS hides (e.g. kpi `status-pills`). Declares intent; the CSS makes it true.

keepTogether.description: Pairs/groups that must never split across a reflow (e.g. a number and its label).

capacity.description: Per-family content capacity — the box-aware generalization of the top-level `capacity`. `axis` names the collection (a focusAxes member); each family key carries soft/hard (and optional min/sweet) element counts for THAT box, plus optional escalateTo. A Strip honestly holds fewer than a Wide.

tags.description: 3-5 search tags from the controlled vocabulary (TAG_GROUPS in lib/components/index.js). The searcher's layer — complementary to Function/Form/Substance, never a restatement of the component's own name/function/form/substance/bucket. Feeds the docs-portal filter and the generated reference. The vocabulary-membership, complementary, and cross-component clustering rules are enforced by validate() and tools/check-ownership.js. See design/design-system.md §7 (Discovery).

purpose.description: Optional: 2-3 sentence rationale for when to reach for this component.

variants.description: Layout-specific modifier names. MUST NOT include universal or semi-universal variants — those are added automatically by effectiveVariants().

excludes.description: Semi-universal variants this layout opts out of (must be a subset of compact / loose / accent).

variantAxes.description: Optional. Groups this layout's variants into orthogonal axes for docs / gallery / variant-chip presentation (e.g. a 'Basemap' axis us/world vs a 'Modifier' axis highlight/robinson/grouped). Members MUST be a subset of variants[]. Purely presentational — the engine routes tokens independently regardless of this grouping.

exclusive.description: True when the members are mutually exclusive — pick exactly one (e.g. the basemap us/world).

default.description: The member that applies when no token in this axis is named (meaningful for exclusive axes).

skeleton.description: Markdown emitted by the scaffolder. Must include the `_class` directive.

docs.description: Deprecated: deep link into a reference doc. Superseded by the generated <name>.docs.md sibling.

example.description: Deprecated: relative path to a snippet file. Superseded by <name>.gallery.md.

whenToUse.description: Bulleted authoring guidance. Each entry has a short title + body sentence. Renders as the 'When to use' section of <name>.docs.md and as the opening prose slide of <name>.gallery.md.

antiPatterns.description: 'Don't' callouts. Same {title, body} shape as whenToUse so the cards-grid meta-slide in the gallery renders consistent bold-title cards. Renders as the 'When NOT to use' section of <name>.docs.md and the anti-patterns slide of <name>.gallery.md.

commonMistakes.description: Authoring-time errors — mistakes made once this component has already been chosen, as opposed to `antiPatterns` (selection-time: don't reach for this component at all). Each entry names one concrete wrong thing an agent/author does and the correct alternative. Renders in the generated docs.md's agent-contract block, above the narrative When-to-use / When-NOT-to-use sections.

mistake.description: The concrete wrong thing an agent/author does while authoring this component.

fix.description: The correct alternative, stated as an instruction.

variantDecisionRule.description: Disambiguates which variant to reach for when the component has more than one — the concrete signal that should drive the pick, not just what each variant looks like (variantDocs.summary covers that). Only meaningful when `variants` has more than one entry (including the implicit no-modifier default); omit for single-shape components. Renders at the top of the generated docs, in the agent-contract block, before the narrative Variants section.

variant.description: A variant token from `variants[]`, or the literal "default" for the no-modifier case.

useWhen.description: The concrete signal — content shape, audience, context — that should drive picking this variant.

dataShapeGuidance.description: Concrete constraints on the SHAPE of author-supplied data, beyond the generic item-count capacity/density budgets — cardinality, formatting/unit consistency, sort order, label length. For data-driven components (chart bucket, series/graph substance, structured comparison layouts). Each entry is one terse, actionable rule, not a paragraph. Omit for prose/single-value components with no external data shape to constrain.

sample.description: Full slide markdown (including the `_class` directive line, with no modifier) for the default-appearance slide of <name>.gallery.md. The skeleton field is the placeholder template for the scaffolder; sample is real prose that demonstrates the component.

stressDoc.description: Required wherever capacity is declared (validate() error since the migration completed); optional elsewhere. The stress-test slide as { summary, sample }: summary is one sentence naming the limit the slide shows; sample is the full slide markdown at the upper content limit. Replaces the legacy stressSample string. (`summary` was named `caption` before the read-as caption channel took that word — 2026-07-11.)

summary.description: One sentence naming the limit shown (surfaced as the specimen caption footer and the Explore caption).

sample.description: Full slide markdown exercising the upper content limit (counted like stressSample by expectedGallerySlideCount()).

specimenVoice.description: Machine-attestable voice flag (2026-07-05 Specimen Book decision). True asserts this manifest's samples passed their migration PR's visual-review fan-out and speak the specimen voice; set ONLY in that PR. Gates the caption footers in galleryPlan(). Absent means unmigrated.

variantDocs.description: Per-variant prose used by the generator. Keys MUST be a subset of variants[]; the validator enforces this.

summary.description: One-sentence summary of what the variant does. (Named `caption` before the read-as caption channel took that word — 2026-07-11.)

sample.description: Full slide markdown (including the `_class` directive line) demonstrating this variant in context.

anatomyBlock.description: ID into the canonical ASCII catalog at tools/ascii-preview.py (e.g. "T7-card-grid-2x2" or "divider-bookend"). The generator resolves this against `python3 tools/ascii-preview.py build` so geometry stays uniform across all components and the canonical block can never drift.

showcase.description: Opt-in metadata for the docs LANDING page (docs/src/pages/index.astro) and its showcase image pipeline (docs/scripts/rasterize-showcase.mjs). Independent of the component portal, which already lists every component automatically. Flagging a component here pulls it into the curated landing highlight reel on the next build (run `npm run showcase` once to rasterize its image).

featured.description: Include this component as a tile in the landing 'every kind of slide' showcase strip.

hero.description: Use this component as the landing hero — its `sample` is shown as the headline source and rendered as the hero slide. Exactly one component should set this.

page.description: 1-based gallery-PDF page to rasterize for the showcase image. Defaults to 2, the manifest `sample` slide.

focusAxes.description: Optional. Focusable axes this layout supports for per-axis `_focus` highlighting — a subset of the focus resolver's SUPPORTED_AXES (lib/transformers/focus.js): a `<table>` body → row/col/cell, a top-level list/grid → item, a code block → line. Scopes the editor's `_focus:` / `_focusSteps:` axis completion per layout.

transform.description: Optional declarative structural-transform rules — the component transform DSL (engineering/decisions/2026-06-29-component-transform-dsl.md). An ordered list of `match → do` rules the engine interprets identically across render paths; NO user JS. The AUTHORITATIVE safety gate is validateTransform() in lib/core/transform-dsl/schema.js (closed element/attribute allowlists, closed selector sub-grammar, known-op/known-capability sets, prototype-pollution defense), run by the manifest loader at load time — this schema only marks the field shape. PROTOTYPE: not yet wired into the render pipeline (§12).

capacity.description: Optional content-capacity contract: how many elements the layout holds along the axis it is built on, so the author/agent picks by content SHAPE and the linter can warn before an overflow. `soft`/`hard` are element counts on `axis` (a focusAxes member): past `soft` the layout begins to crowd (soft warning); past `hard` it overflows / loses legibility (overflow warning). Advisory only — never blocks. Counted approximately at authoring time (lib/authoring/lint-core.js `countPrimaryCollection`) and exactly at render time (lib/core/collections.js). See engineering/decisions/2026-06-17-content-capacity-contract.md.

axis.description: The collection that drives crowding — MUST be a focusAxes member when focusAxes is declared. `item` = top-level list/grid entries, `row`/`col`/`cell` = table, `line` = code lines.

min.description: Below this the layout looks starved (advisory; not warned).

sweet.description: The ideal count surfaced to the author/agent.

soft.description: Past this the layout begins to crowd → soft warning.

hard.description: Past this the layout overflows / loses legibility → overflow warning.

escalateTo.description: Actionable fix the warning prints — sibling component names and/or 'split across slides'. UNIVERSAL RULE: 'split across slides' (autosplit / the Fit Ladder's SPLIT move) operates ONLY at a portrait/square @size — portrait, story, mobile, square. In a wide/landscape box, collapse + shed resolve overflow before split is reached, so the engine skips autosplit there (lattice-emulator.js) and lint:deck warns on `autosplit: on` + a landscape @size (rule autosplit-landscape-noop). The orientation boundary is lib/authoring/lint-core.js PORTRAIT_SIZES; see engineering/decisions/2026-06-22-the-fit-spine.md §3 + 2026-06-23-read-across-carousel.md.

note.description: One-line human consequence of overflowing (reused in the generated docs line).

density.description: Optional prose-density budget (phase 2 of the content-capacity contract) — how many WORDS each element along `axis` gets before the slide loses brevity, so the author/agent writes tight and the reviewer can flag verbosity. Where `capacity` budgets the element COUNT, `density` budgets the words-per-element. `soft` is the editorial target surfaced to the author (a label + short clause, not a sentence); `hard` is the evidence-clamped overflow ceiling (set just below where rendering actually overflows — see tools/calibrate-density.js). Advisory only — surfaces as a review SUGGESTION (lib/authoring/review-core.js), never a lint warning, so the stress galleries stay free. See engineering/decisions/2026-06-30-prose-density-budget.md.

axis.description: The collection whose ELEMENTS carry the budgeted prose. Defaults to `capacity.axis` when omitted. Unlike capacity, NOT tied to focusAxes — focusAxes governs _focus highlighting (a ledger may highlight as table rows) while density counts the markdown the author writes (a ledger authored as a bullet list is the `item` axis; glossary is the canonical case). The only axis guard is measurability in the sample. Per-element word counting is currently implemented for `item` and `row` only; validate() rejects the others (col/cell/line) so a block can't validate yet silently never fire.

soft.description: Words per element — the editorial target surfaced to the author/agent. Past this the element begins to crowd → soft suggestion.

hard.description: Words per element — the EDITORIAL maximum: past this the element reads as a wall of text. This is NOT the physical overflow point (the Fit Spine owns that, far higher) — it is clamped to stay safely UNDER the measured geometric ceiling (tools/calibrate-density.js), so the suggestion never claims a break that won't happen. Always ≥ soft; the gap between soft and hard is the editorial 'reads well' → 'reads heavy' band.

note.description: One-line human consequence of over-writing the element (reused in the generated Density docs line and the suggestion message).

domSelector.description: CSS selector, scoped within the axis's clip-cell/section, that resolves to this component's LIVE RENDERED DOM elements for `axis` — only needed when it differs from the universal per-axis default (item → `ul > li` / `ol > li`; row → `table tbody > tr`). A component whose own transform retags or rewraps the axis elements (e.g. split-compare's options become `.option` divs, not `<li>`) MUST declare this or a live-preview consumer (the Fix-Me overlay's drill-down) silently finds nothing and falls back to a coarser highlight. Verified by a render-time coverage test, not just declared — see engineering/decisions/2026-07-10-overflow-cause-highlighting.md §10.

families.description: Opt-in modifier-family groups this component joins (only the per-layout families — bucket-scoped families apply automatically from the bucket, so declaring them here is rejected). The enum is the source of truth for the opt-in set; lib/components/index.js OPT_IN_FAMILY_NAMES must match (sync-gated by test/unit/components/schema-source-of-truth.test.js).

dataCompletion.description: When true, the layout renders author-supplied data to completion (no sampling/truncation) — read by the docs portal and authoring guidance.

split.description: The Fit Ladder carousel recipe: when a slide of this layout OVERFLOWS (deck-level `autosplit: on`), lib/core/auto-split.js hands the section to lib/core/carousel.js carouselize() with this recipe, re-authoring the read-across as a cover → windowed sequence. The strategy enum is the source of truth; CAROUSEL_STRATEGIES in lib/core/carousel.js must carry exactly these keys (sync-gated). Historically this field was undocumented and unvalidated — a typo'd strategy silently fell through (or, worse, hit an Object.prototype member).

strategy.description: Which carouselize() splitter re-authors the overflowing section. See lib/core/carousel.js for what each strategy parses and emits.

axis.description: The collection axis the paginating strategies window over (overrides capacity.axis for the re-authored split body).

perPage.description: How many members each windowed page holds (strategies that window: cover-rows, cover-decision, cover-paginate).

intro.description: The cover's kicker line introducing the windowed sequence (e.g. "The reasoning").

family.description: Free-form label grouping recipes in docs/notes (not read by carouselize).

roles.description: The page roles the strategy emits, for docs (e.g. ["cover", "points"]); not read by carouselize.

note.description: Maintainer note: why this recipe, its preconditions, and the decision doc that introduced it.
